summary:
FieldShift is an agriculture decision-support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps farmers explore smarter crop-rotation strategies by combining farm information, crop characteristics, farmer priorities, and NASA Earth observation data.

The platform compares three approaches: existing crop rotation, soil restoration, and climate resilience. It considers factors such as temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, soil conditions, water requirements, and potential agricultural risks to help farmers understand the benefits and trade-offs of different strategies.

FieldShift integrates NASA POWER climate data and NASA Earthdata services, including Common Metadata Repository (CMR) granule discovery. It also provides interactive farm mapping, what-if climate scenarios, soil intelligence, crop information, and AI-assisted insights.

Our goal is to make Earth observation data more accessible and useful for agricultural decision-making, helping farmers explore sustainable and climate-aware farming practices.
details:
Project Overview

FieldShift is a NASA Earth observation-powered agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers explore crop-rotation strategies and understand how environmental conditions can influence agricultural planning.

Traditional crop planning can be challenging because farmers must consider soil conditions, crop requirements, water availability, changing weather patterns, and long-term soil health. FieldShift brings these considerations together in one platform.

How It Works

Farmers can explore farm properties, provide agricultural information, select farming priorities, and examine available environmental observations.

The platform compares three crop-rotation strategies:

  1. Existing Rotation: establishes a baseline using the farmer's current crop-rotation approach.
  2. Soil Restoration: explores crop sequences and practices that support soil protection, crop diversity, and nutrient cycling.
  3. Climate Resilience : evaluates alternative crop sequences against climate-related considerations such as temperature, precipitation, and water requirements.

FieldShift uses available NASA Earth observation information to support its analysis. NASA POWER provides numerical climate indicators, while NASA Earthdata CMR helps discover relevant satellite data granules. The platform also includes soil intelligence, an interactive farm map, a bare-field detector, pest and disease cycle tracking, and what-if climate scenarios.

Technology and Tools

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite
  • Backend: Node.js, Express, TypeScript
  • Database and Authentication: Supabase, PostgreSQL
  • AI: Google Gemini
  • Visualization: Three.js and React Three Fiber
  • Deployment: Vercel
  • Earth observation resources: NASA POWER, NASA Earthdata CMR, MODIS, SMAP, and GPM

Creativity and Innovation

FieldShift combines agricultural decision support with Earth observation data and interactive scenario exploration. Instead of presenting satellite information as isolated scientific measurements, it connects available environmental indicators with crop characteristics, farmer priorities, and alternative crop-rotation strategies.

The three-strategy comparison gives farmers a way to examine different agricultural approaches and understand their potential benefits, limitations, and trade-offs.

Intended Impact

Our goal is to make NASA Earth science information more accessible to agricultural decision-making. FieldShift aims to support more informed crop planning, encourage soil-conscious farming practices, and help farmers consider climate-related agricultural risks.

The platform is designed as a decision-support tool. Its recommendations are exploratory and depend on the availability, resolution, quality, and limitations of the underlying data.
